interest: Shows postwar US-Japan disputes over cultural restitution, and the preservation of a Manchukuo historical manuscript amid Chinese Nationalist pressure.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.412 (covering December 1945 to August 1948) documents United States policy and diplomatic actions concerning historical relics, manuscripts, and the restitution and replacement of cultural property associated with wartime Japan. The file centers on three distinct episodes: first, diplomatic exchanges in December 1945 between Washington, the U.S. mission in Bangkok, and SCAP regarding the identification and return of a sacred, seven-layered Buddhist relic transferred from Siam to Japan under wartime duress; second, an in-depth March 1948 policy memorandum analyzing inter-agency disputes within the Far Eastern Commission (FEC) and SANACC over policy paper SFE 202/2 ('Replacement of Cultural Objects'), pitting the State Department's advocacy for Asian Allies' cultural restitution against the Army's Civil Affairs Division (CAD); and third, a protracted May–August 1948 dispute in Peiping involving Consul General O. Edmund Clubb, who sheltered an unpublished Japanese galley-proof manuscript of 'Ten Years History of Manchoukuo' by Professor Masajiro Takigawa from confiscation by Chinese Nationalist authorities, enabling its microfilming by the Library of Congress before returning the original to its Japanese custodians.

subfiles.about: The State Department directs the U.S. political adviser in Bangkok to ascertain the Siamese government's wishes regarding the return of a sacred Buddha relic taken to Japan during World War II.
subfiles.summary: Acheson tells Bangkok that SCAP holds a sacred Buddha relic taken to Japan under duress, asking Thai views on return.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Acting Secretary of State Acheson to Bangkok on Siamese Buddha Relic

subfiles.about: The U.S. mission in Bangkok reports that the Thai Government formally requests the return from Japan of the sacred Buddha relic given under duress.
subfiles.from: Charles W. Yost (U.S. Chargé d'Affaires, Bangkok)
subfiles.summary: Yost reports Thailand strongly wants the sacred Buddha relic, surrendered under wartime duress, returned from Japan.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Yost (Bangkok) on Siamese Request for Return of Sacred Buddha Relic

subfiles.about: The Thai Government describes the seven-layered stupa housing the Buddha relic and insists that all layers be returned intact from Japan.
subfiles.from: Charles W. Yost (U.S. Chargé d'Affaires, Bangkok)
subfiles.summary: Yost details the Buddha relic's seven protective stupa layers, and Siam's request its full set be returned intact.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Yost (Bangkok) Detailing Seven Stupa Layers of Buddha Relic

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum examines inter-agency disagreements over policy paper SFE 202/2 regarding the replacement of cultural objects looted and destroyed by Japan.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Fearey (Office of Northeast Asian Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Fearey refutes Army objections to replacing Allied cultural property lost to Japan, recommending State maintain support for Allied restitution rights.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Fearey to Allison on State Department Position on Replacement of Cultural Objects (SFE 202/2)
subfiles.to: John M. Allison (Office of Northeast Asian Affairs)

subfiles.about: Consul General Clubb transmits an unpublished Japanese galley-proof manuscript on Manchukuo's history to Washington, recommending it be microfilmed before return.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb (American Consul General, Peiping)
subfiles.summary: Clubb forwards an unpublished Manchukuo history manuscript, resisting Chinese demands to surrender it, suggesting State microfilm it before return.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 113 from Clubb (Peiping) Transmitting Japanese Manuscript 'Ten Years History of Manchoukuo'

subfiles.about: Translator Sakimura details the authorship, provenance, and attempted police seizure of Takigawa's manuscript on Manchukuo.
subfiles.from: Shigeki Sakimura (Translator, American Consulate General, Peiping)
subfiles.summary: Sakimura recounts Prof. Takigawa's Manchukuo history manuscript's journey to Peiping, and police pressure to surrender it, stopped by US consular intervention.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Sakimura on the Provenance and History of the Manchukuo Manuscript
subfiles.to: O. Edmund Clubb (American Consul General, Peiping)

subfiles.about: Mayor Ho Ssu-yuan requests that the American Consulate surrender the Manchukuo manuscript on behalf of Nationalist authorities in Mukden.
subfiles.summary: Peiping's Mayor demands Clubb surrender the Takigawa manuscript, alleging it holds Manchukuo state secrets smuggled out by a consulate employee.
subfiles.title: Translation of Letter from Peiping Mayor Ho Ssu-yuan to Clubb Requesting Surrender of Manuscript
subfiles.to: O. Edmund Clubb (American Consul General, Peiping)

subfiles.about: Consul General Clubb refuses to deliver the Manchukuo manuscript to Peiping municipal authorities without specific identification and legal justification.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb (American Consul General, Peiping)
subfiles.summary: Clubb refuses to surrender the manuscript, noting it is private property with no sign of being an official Manchukuo secret.
subfiles.title: Letter from Clubb to Mayor Ho Ssu-yuan Refusing Unsubstantiated Surrender of Manuscript

subfiles.about: The State Department reports that the Library of Congress has microfilmed Takigawa's manuscript and that the original is being returned to Peiping.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Acting Secretary of State / W. E. Jenkins)
subfiles.summary: State finds the Takigawa manuscript contains no secrets, has it microfilmed by the Library of Congress, and returns the original.
subfiles.title: Despatch from State Department to Peiping Consulate General on Microfilming of Manchukuo Manuscript
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Peiping

subfiles.about: Consul Touchette reports a renewed Chinese Nationalist request for the Manchukuo manuscript and urges its prompt return if microfilmed.
subfiles.summary: Touchette reports Peiping authorities renew their demand for the Takigawa manuscript, asking that it be returned once microfilmed.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 268 from Touchette (Peiping) on Renewed Chinese Demand for Manuscript

subfiles.about: Secretary Marshall inquires whether the Peiping consulate objects to the Library of Congress microfilming the non-secret manuscript.
subfiles.summary: Marshall tells Peiping the Takigawa manuscript holds no secrets, and asks if the consulate objects to Library of Congress microfilming.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 132 from Secretary of State Marshall to Peiping on Library of Congress Microfilming

subfiles.about: The Peiping Consulate General agrees to microfilming the manuscript and requests that the physical copy be returned to China.
subfiles.summary: Touchette agrees to the Library of Congress microfilming the Takigawa manuscript, and asks that it then be returned to Peiping.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Touchette (Peiping) Concurring with Microfilming and Requesting Return of Manuscript
